title: Black Behi pechay: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Black Behi pechay: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Black Behi pechay is a pechay variety from B.M. Domingo. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: Black Behi is a registered pechay variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1970. B.M. Domingo bred it. It takes 30 to 35 days from sowing to harvest.

items: **Days to harvest:** 30 to 35 days from sowing to harvest.

blocks.text: Key facts about Black Behi pechay
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Black Behi pechay takes 30 to 35 days from sowing to harvest. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
The registry gives no pest or disease ratings for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit pechay fields most often: [bacterial soft rot](/diseases/soft-rot), [black rot of cabbage](/diseases/black-rot), [cabbage webworm](/pests/cabbage-webworm), [clubroot](/diseases/clubroot), [diamondback moth](/pests/diamondback-moth). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant Black Behi pechay

Pechay is ready in about a month, so it fits small plots and quick cash. Pick a variety that bolts late in the heat and stands rain. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng gulay](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-gulay).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 30 to 35 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Black Behi?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
